page.overview:
Who is Aegyptosaurus?

is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in Africa during the Late Cretaceous period around 100-94 million years ago. It lived along the shores of an ancient sea in what is now the Sahara Desert. This large dinosaur is actually a smaller relative of the gigantic Argentinosaurus from South America. During the time Aegyptosaurus lived, Africa and South America were still connected and it may have moved to this North African location over many thousands of years, involving into a smaller version of their South American relatives, though this is debated.

Aegyptosaurus is yet another spectacular specimen temporarily lost during WWII. Discovered in the same location as Spinosaurus, it may have been lost in the same bombing of Germany that may have destroyed evidence of other specimens.

Aegyptosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.
